newsitem.title: Australia: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 1.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Melbourne centre Mark Bradtke was cleared by basketball's world governing body FIBA to play in the National Basketball League this weekend, after missing last weekend's match against South East Melbourne. Melbourne remains under investigation for playing radtke last Friday against Adelaide, and may lose the points for the win is found to have breached player rules. Page 19.

Australian tennis players Jason Stoltenberg and Sandon Stolle won their matches in the first round of the AT&T Challenge yesterday. Seventh seed Stoltenberg beat Zimbabwe's Byron Black 2-6 6-3 6-4, while Stolle won over Frenchman Jerome Hanquez, 6-3 6-2. age 19.

A charge against Essendon defender Dean Wallis was dismissed by the Australia Football League Tribunal last night after a field umpire said he was coerced into writing the wrong date on the charge sheet. AFL operations manager Ian Collins has summoned theparties involved in the reporting process to an urgent meeting today. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

News Ltd and Cronulla yesterday rejected a claim by former Cronulla board member that the Super League club might be forced to slash its budget in the next 18 months, after News Ltd's annual A$2.5 million guarantee expires at the end of next year. Super Legue chief executive John Ribot said the guarantee would be renewed with the franchise next year. Page 52.

Australian Rugby League referees will only acknowledge the comments of team captains during matches, in an effort to curb the recent rise of backchatting to referees. The Australian Rugby League's Captains Committee met with communications manager Geoff Carr yesterday and agreed to a code to restrict player challenges of match officials. Page 52.

Sydney centre half-forward Jason Mooney was cited by the Australian Football League for misconduct yesterday. Already given a four-match suspension on Monday for headbutting Hawthorn's Brendan Krummel, Mooney was cited for poking Krummel in the eye in thesame incident. Page 52.
THE AGE

Carlton United Breweries has announced a A$10 million sponsorship program to help new and established Australian athletes prepare for the 1998 Winter Olympics in Nagano, Japan and the Sydney 2000 Olympics. Page B6.

North Melbourne AFL player Dean Laidley will miss four weeks after tearing his thigh during training at Waverley Park on Tuesday. John Langmire is also in doubt for Saturday's game against Hawthorn, due to a hamstring strain. Page B8.

South Melbourne President George Vasilopoulos responded yesterday to Soccer Australia's efforts to de-ethnicise the game. He said he was "sick and tired" of the anti-ethnic forces in Australian soccer and said ethnic communities were entitled to assert thmselves in the sport. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Three-time world 500cc motorcycle champion Michael Doohan has called for tighter crowd control during the Spanish motorcycle grand prix on Sunday. Last year, thousands of spectators invaded restricted areas and ran on to the edge of the track during the last lap to cheer on Spaniard Alex Creville, who crashed on the last turn, giving Doohan the victory. Page 87.

Champion pole-vaulter Emma George won an international competition in Hiroshima Japan yesterday, clearing 4.20 metres, 35cm short of her world record. The competition saw George try a 14-step run-up for the first time. Page 89.

South Australian cyclist Luke Roberts faces a possible fine and/or suspension for failing to submit to a drug test while competing in Italy. The Australian Cycling Federation said there were mitigating circumstances - Roberts pulled out of the 160 kilomete race before the finish, and was unaware that he had been selected for a random test. Page 89.

Victoria University's netball team upset the fourth-ranked Palladians last night. After three narrow losses in a row, Victoria University took advantage of an injury-depleted Palladians side to win 54-41. Page 83.

Australian tennis players, Annabel Ellwood and Rachel McQuillan were both knocked out of the Croatian Open yesterday. Ellwood was beaten by Silvija Talaja 6-2 6-2, and McQuillan lost to Mirjana Lucic 6-2 6-2. Page 83. -- In a letter to AFL chief executive officer Wayne Jackson yesterday, Collingwood fitness coach Mark McKeon called for the AFL to demand that all players wear knee supports in matches,. Page 94.
